origins.section: 8.2 An Event Goes to Its Source's Logger, and a Channel Without One Writes Nothing
8.5 A Realm Filter Narrows the Log and Drops Everything It Doesn't Name
8.6 A Late Answer Is Counted, Not Logged, by the MUX
8.7 A Bridge to SLF4J Sits After the Filter and Keeps Each Event Whole

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-channel-without-logger: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-channel-without-logger: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-channel-without-logger: Section 8.2 decides c: 'Q2 calls their setLogger(logger, realm) only when their own element has a logger attribute. Without it they drop every event', and the nochannel run shows 'no event from the channel or the packager'.
recorded.prompt:q-realm-filter-deploy-error: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-realm-filter-deploy-error: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-realm-filter-deploy-error: Section 8.5 decides a: Q2 'reports a descriptor that fails to deploy, at start-up or later, under Q2.system', the filter drops unnamed realms 'for every listener after it', and 'a typo in 20_host_mux.xml makes the MUX vanish without a word in the log'.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval-evidence: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval-evidence: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval-evidence: Section 8.6 decides c: the late answer 'went to the MUX's <unhandled> queue ... QMUX writes no event for it; it only counts it', and 'rx_unhandled counts only when the MUX has an <unhandled> queue', which the stem provides.
recorded.prompt:q-library-warning: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-warning: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-warning: Section 8.7 decides c: with no binding, Q2's attempt 'fails quietly' on a current JDK (seen on Java 21), and 'SLF4J falls back to a logger that discards everything, so the library's messages go nowhere'.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-channel-without-logger:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-channel-without-logger:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-channel-without-logger:a: Section 8.2 refutes it directly: 'The adaptor's own logger covers only the adaptor', and the nochannel run has no connect, send or receive.
recorded.prompt:q-channel-without-logger:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-channel-without-logger:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-channel-without-logger:b: Section 8.2 refutes it: an event created by a Log 'is also marked to honour its source's logger, so when the Log has none ... it does not fall back to Q2. It goes nowhere', and the nochannel run logged nothing from the channel.
recorded.prompt:q-channel-without-logger:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-channel-without-logger:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-channel-without-logger:d: Section 8.2's full run logs connect, send and receive x2 for a purchase whose answer came back, so with a logger the channel writes events for successful traffic, not only for failures; without one it writes nothing.
recorded.prompt:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:b: Section 8.5 refutes it directly: 'Q2 keeps watching deploy/ and reports a descriptor that fails to deploy, at start-up or later'.
recorded.prompt:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:c: Section 8.5's table lists 'Q2.system dropped', and the advice 'add Q2.system to the list' shows Q2.system gets no exception.
recorded.prompt:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-realm-filter-deploy-error:d: By short inference from 8.5 and the 8.9 table ('drops events by realm (the part before the first /)'), the filter judges only the realm, and the deploy error, which carries no ISO message, is dropped 'without a word'.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval-evidence:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval-evidence:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval-evidence:a: Section 8.6 refutes it directly: 'QMUX writes no event for it; it only counts it.'
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval-evidence:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval-evidence:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval-evidence:b: Section 8.6 refutes it: the answer 'arrived after the wait was over, found nobody waiting for its key', so it never reaches the request that already returned null.
recorded.prompt:q-late-approval-evidence:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-late-approval-evidence:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-late-approval-evidence:d: Sections 8.6 and 8.9 separate the two counters ('One request ended with no answer (rx_expired=1), and one answer matched nothing (rx_unhandled=1)'), so the late answer is counted in rx_unhandled; but rx_expired does rise for the same request, so a reader has to see that it counts the request, not the answer.
recorded.prompt:q-library-warning:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-warning:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-warning:a: Section 8.7 refutes it: the binding attempt fails on Java 21 and works only when the JVM is started with --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED, which the stem's command line lacks.
recorded.prompt:q-library-warning:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-warning:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-warning:b: Section 8.7 refutes it directly: once the binding fails, 'the library's messages go nowhere', so nothing collects them under any realm.
recorded.prompt:q-library-warning:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-library-warning:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-library-warning:d: Section 8.7 refutes the reason: the bridge is 'jPOS into SLF4J', and library output would reach Q2 through Q2's own SLF4J binding (under slf4j:: realms), not through a bridge.

gates.says: each of the 4 questions keys exactly 1 of its distinct options and every option carries the sentence its reader is shown
each of the 4 questions cites a passage the ledger still digests to the value this exercise was built from
